liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- Around 1:50 in the second track, a listener hears what might be a bit of Lovelight [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Speed Limit**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [14]
- **Neil Cassidy Raps**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1965-11-01.sbd.bershaw.5417.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 2 songs; 12 min; rated 3.32/5 by 19 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer hears Jerry's guitar riffs as sluggish on this tape; The first few minutes have unexplained parts, possibly from open microphones scattered around an acid test; Playing gets hot after about six minutes, and a trumpet is audible near the four-minute mark [3][9]

## Around the show

- Recording was released as a flexi-disc in the first printing of The Dead Book [1]
- Neal Cassady can be heard speaking, but only in short snippets [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1965-11-01.sbd.bershaw.5417.sbeok.shnf**: Studio recording from a Prankster production tape, circa late 1965, credited to Neal Cassady and the Warlocks; Lawrence Schiller's original record sampled this tape; the group on it was Fire and Ice, from LA; Material seems to come from an unreleased studio session; the sleeve's Acid Test reference points to a Kesey recording, perhaps January 29, 1966 [1][8]
